sanitized_dependency_sequence: A human-authored scheduled instruction tells the shared orchestrator to check network health and escalate critical findings to the configured CTO role.
The orchestrator attempts a direct session send to that role.
The tool returns an error that no session exists for the label.
The same orchestrator inserts a high-priority escalation row addressed to the CTO role in the designed event table.
The returned row has no processing timestamp.
Later selected records show the same orchestrator reading or repeating the escalation state; none is a receipt or dependent action by the named CTO role.
architecture_and_authorization: The cron instruction explicitly requests escalation to the CTO role.
The repository describes an operator-facing multi-agent operating system, and its configuration explicitly assigns both roles and their triggers.
The runbook defines the event queue, pending-event checks and escalation-path verification as intended operations.
The selected session records are under an archive path; current activity is not inferred from them.

alternatives.designed_monitoring: Confirmed. The human cron explicitly asks for the health check and escalation.
alternatives.single_operator_automation: Dominant. One configured system and one shared orchestrator create the attempted send and fallback row.
alternatives.repeated_test_or_retry: Supported by later same-orchestrator attempts and monitor reads.
alternatives.shared_state_or_observer_contamination: Later references belong to the same orchestrator reading its own notes/outbox state, not a foreign recipient.
alternatives.independent_recipient: Not established; the direct send failed and no recipient-session record was located in the bounded checks.
